scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

Most of my week revolves around Sunday service — communion, the same people, every single week. A lot of my closest friends are from that same church community too. Do you think being that deep inside one community makes it harder to think for yourself about what is actually right?

Being deeply involved in a community, such as a church, can both support and challenge independent thinking. Here's a structured summary of the considerations and conclusions: 1. **Understanding Independent Thinking**: It involves evaluating information, considering different perspectives, and making decisions based on personal reasoning rather than conforming to the group. 2. **Influence of Community**: - **Positive Aspects**: Provides support, diverse viewpoints, and encouragement for critical thinking. - **Challenges**: Risk of "groupthink," where harmony is prioritized over individual reasoning, and social norms that may limit autonomy. 3. **Confirmation Bias and Echo Chambers**: Communities may reinforce existing beliefs, leading to an echo chamber effect where dissenting opinions are dismissed. 4. **Leadership Role**: Leaders who encourage open dialogue and critical thinking can foster an environment conducive to independent thought. 5. **Cognitive Dissonance**: The discomfort from conflicting beliefs or actions can prompt changes to align with the community, potentially stifling personal reasoning. 6. **Personal Reflection**: Engaging in self-reflection and seeking diverse viewpoints can help balance community influence with personal autonomy. 7. **Support System**: Having relationships with people of different perspectives can broaden one's view and aid in evaluating what's right. 8. **Conclusion**: While community involvement can provide a strong support system, it's crucial to seek diverse perspectives, engage in self-reflection, and ensure the community supports open dialogue and critical examination of beliefs to maintain independent thinking. In essence, the key to maintaining independent thought within a community lies in fostering an environment that values diverse perspectives and encourages personal reflection.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being too much or not in this situation with my boyfriend. Let me start by understanding the scenario. I have a son who's 12 and he wants to play football on weekends. I was thinking of asking my boyfriend to help with the transportation because he works full-time from 7 am to 7 pm, and I have a weekend job from 9 am to 12 pm. We don't live together, but we're local, so we're always in and out of each other's homes. Initially, I thought of asking my boyfriend to pay for the football, but when I mentioned it to my mom, she told me it's my responsibility, not his. So, I ended up paying for it myself, but to afford it, I had to extend my work hours to 9 am to 5 pm. Then, I asked my boyfriend if he could pick up and drop off my son on weekends. He looked uncomfortable and suggested that my son's dad could do it. I snapped at him, pointing out that my son's dad lives in South London, while we're in North London, and that the journey would take an hour for my son's dad, but only 15 minutes for my boyfriend. I also asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did, he wouldn't mind doing small stuff like this for me. He got really angry, saying he has to work longer hours to support me and my son, and that he wants to use his weekends to go to football games and chill since I'm not home anyway. He suggested we break up because I'm putting too many responsibilities on him. I was shocked and told him it's over a bloody football game and that he needs to get real. My son then went to my mom, and she had a heart-to-heart with him, leading her to call me and tell me I'm out of line. So, the question is: Am I being too much? Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) here? First, I need to consider the dynamics of the relationship. We don't live together, but we're local and spend a lot of time at each other's homes. I have a son, and he's been in my life for three years. I'm asking him to help with my son's activities, which seems reasonable, but he's pushing back, saying he works long hours and wants to use his weekends for himself. On one hand, I'm trying to manage my responsibilities as a parent and a worker, and I'm asking for help from someone who's been a significant part of my life. On the other hand, he's feeling burdened by the additional responsibilities and wants to maintain his own time. I also need to consider the role of my mom in this. She told me it's my responsibility to pay for my son's activities, which influenced my decision to extend my work hours. However, when I asked my boyfriend for help, he felt it was too much, leading to an argument and his suggestion to break up. I'm wondering if I'm overstepping by asking him for help, especially since my mom expects me to handle it alone. Is it fair to ask him to take on more responsibilities when he's already working long hours? Or is it reasonable to expect some support from someone who's been in my life for three years? Also, the fact that my son went to my mom and that she told me I'm out of line adds another layer to this. It seems like my mom supports my boyfriend's stance, which might make me feel isolated. I'm trying to balance my responsibilities as a parent and worker with the expectations in the relationship. Am I being too demanding? Or is my boyfriend not understanding the pressures I'm under? I think it's important to communicate openly about expectations and responsibilities in the relationship. Maybe setting boundaries and discussing how to support each other without feeling overwhelmed would help. In the end, I need to evaluate whether my actions are reasonable or if I'm placing undue pressure on my boyfriend, leading to the breakdown of the relationship.
